<explanation>
Based on the provided file tree and README, I'll explain how to create a comprehensive system design diagram for the Moby Project, which is a complex containerization system.

1. Main Components Overview
The system design diagram should be organized into these major sections:

a. Core Components:
- Container Runtime (daemon)
- API Server
- Builder System
- Network Stack (libnetwork)
- Storage/Layer System
- Volume Management
- Plugin System

b. External Interfaces:
- Client API
- Registry Integration
- Plugin Interface
- Host System Integration

2. Detailed Component Breakdown

The diagram should use the following structure:

```
[Client Interface Layer]
       ↓
[API Server (api/*)] ← → [Authentication/Authorization]
       ↓
[Daemon Core (daemon/*)]
       ↓
[Component Subsystems]
├── Builder (builder/*)
├── Container Runtime (container/*)
├── Network Stack (libnetwork/*)
├── Storage Layer (layer/*)
├── Volume Management (volume/*)
└── Plugin System (plugin/*)
```

3. Key Relationships to Highlight

a. Data Flow:
- Show API request flow from client through API server to daemon
- Illustrate container lifecycle management
- Demonstrate storage and network interactions

b. Integration Points:
- Container runtime to host system
- Network integration with host
- Storage driver interface
- Plugin system extensibility

4. Color Coding and Symbols

Use the following scheme:
- Blue: Core services (daemon, API)
- Green: Resource management (network, storage)
- Orange: Build system
- Purple: Plugin/extension system
- Gray: External interfaces

5. Implementation Details

The diagram should include:
- REST API endpoints (from api/*)
- Container runtime components (from daemon/*)
- Network stack (from libnetwork/*)
- Storage drivers (from layer/*)
- Volume management (from volume/*)

6. Specific Technical Elements

Include these key technical components:
- containerd integration
- OCI runtime specification
- Network drivers (bridge, overlay, etc.)
- Storage drivers (overlay2, btrfs, etc.)
- Volume plugins
- Security subsystems (apparmor, seccomp)

7. Cross-Cutting Concerns

Highlight these aspects:
- Security boundaries
- Logging system
- Event system
- Metrics collection
- Error handling

8. Legend and Documentation

Include:
- Component type indicators
- Interface definitions
- Data flow markers
- Security boundary indicators
- Version compatibility notes

The diagram should maintain a balance between showing the complexity of the system while keeping it understandable. Focus on the major interaction patterns and data flows, with the ability to drill down into specific subsystems as needed.

Remember to emphasize the modular nature of the system, as this is a key principle of the Moby Project, showing how components can be swapped out or modified while maintaining the overall system architecture.

This diagram will serve as both a technical reference and an architectural guide for developers working with the system.

</explanation>
